source.title: Probing the Geometry of Color Representations in Multilingual Language Models
source.authors: Pablo Loyola; Edison Marrese-Taylor; Andrés Hoyos-Idrobo

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. No apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures perceptual alignment and cross-lingual symmetry, and concludes that multilingual color geometry is only partly shared and reflects linguistic rather than necessarily perceptual structure. Its comparisons do not test convergence between independently trained models as they scale.
record.gate_note: The study does not compare pairwise representations of independently trained models, sweep model size or capability, or test vision-language alignment. Its geometric comparisons are model-to-LAB and between language-specific representations within a model. Color-task probe accuracies are functional results, not measurements of the convergence named in the claim, so they are not rows. The paper’s cited findings from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study never compares representations of different models with each other. Its P1 analysis aligns each model to a fixed CIE–LAB reference. Its P2 analysis compares language-specific kernels inside a single model. Neither measures convergence between independently trained models, across seeds, across modalities on paired data, via mappings, or via shared features. The paper does argue that 'platonic' universality in color is linguistic rather than perceptual (Sec. 6.1, 6.4). That argument rests on within-model cross-lingual congruence, not cross-model alignment, so it does not test V7's claim about what explains inter-model convergence. P1 pooling and subset sensitivity concern model-to-LAB alignment, not measured inter-model convergence, so it is not a V6 test either. These are related constructs, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors also stress a dissociation at the output layer: cross-lingual symmetry persists while perceptual alignment collapses. They report that effective rank tracks both axes (r about 0.76–0.99) and that probe accuracy peaks where LAB alignment peaks. They present this as refining, not testing, the Platonic hypothesis: universality in color is distributional or linguistic rather than perceptual.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures model-to-perceptual-reference alignment and within-model cross-language kernel congruence, rather than comparing independently trained models’ representations as a function of scale or capability.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and description subset affect perceptual alignment; matched-n sampling reduces the Munsell advantage; pooling affects results, with last-token pooling unstable and model-dependent. The paper uses CKA with an RBF kernel and median bandwidth heuristic, and states that other bandwidth choices were not evaluated.

fits_no_version.finding: CKA alignment of LM color-description geometry to CIE–LAB is weak (about 0.0–0.2). It peaks in layers 0–6 and drops about 80% by the final layer. It depends on dataset (Munsell vs MLMC; matched-n control), on description type (BCT peak about 3–4× non-BCT), and on pooling (last-token collapses alignment for Gemma and Mistral but raises the peak for Llama and Qwen).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Text-only LM representations are only weakly and transiently aligned with a perceptual reference geometry (CIE–LAB for color). The measured alignment depends on layer, input wording and pooling.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-model cross-lingual kernel congruence on matched colors is 0.56–0.71 at embeddings. It falls to 0.29–0.56 at the final layer, with model-dependent mid-layer dips (e.g. Gemma-9B 0.127). The authors read the shared structure as distributional, not perceptual.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a multilingual LM, representational geometry for the same concepts in different languages is largely shared at early layers and diverges with depth.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to color and the reported datasets. Absolute alignment can depend on sampling density; the study does not evaluate alternative kernel bandwidths and notes that alternative similarity measures could give complementary perspectives. The text does not report uncertainty for several tabulated comparisons. Cross-lingual congruence is not independent-model convergence, and the proposed linguistic explanation is not causally tested.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports effective-rank correlations and color-task probe results, but these do not directly measure the convergence named by the versions. No other claim-relevant result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: No pairwise alignment between independently trained models and no scale or capability sweep. Model profiles are only compared qualitatively.
No image–caption paired alignment. PaliGemma2 is only analysed on text color descriptions.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests.
No feature or circuit recurrence analysis.
Metric, pooling and data dependence is shown only for alignment to LAB, not for inter-model convergence.
No inter-model alignment level or plateau is measured. The causal attribution to shared linguistic data is argued, not tested, and only for within-model cross-lingual structure.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' and its V6/V7 labels are rejected. The rows measure model-to-LAB and within-model cross-language similarity, not convergence between models. The paper's argument against Platonic 'world-grounded' universality is an interpretation of within-model data, not an inter-model test. One factual row error: r16's peak layer should be 27.

versions.untested_parts: No independent-model alignment comparison or scale/performance sweep.
No paired image-caption representation alignment or cross-modal scale/performance comparison.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No recurrence of interpretable features or circuits is measured.

The study examines changes across datasets, description subsets, and pooling choices, but does not compare a broad set of alternative similarity metrics or kernel bandwidths. It does not test out-of-distribution inputs.

The study measures cross-language geometry within individual models, not alignment among independently trained models. It does not causally test whether shared training data or objectives produce the observed structure.

rows.operation_detail: Layerwise normalized CKA between model color-description geometry and CIE–LAB
rows.value: Scores peak between layers 0–6, depending on model depth, then drop substantially—by about 80% by the final layer.
rows.note: The paper reports this pattern across model families; no per-model values are stated in this result.
rows.check: Model-to-CIE–LAB CKA is alignment to a perceptual reference, not alignment between models. It cannot show V6's metric or data dependence of inter-model convergence. In r16 the peak layer is wrong: Table 5 gives 27 for Mistral-7B non-BCT, not 0. In r3 the subject should be the four text-only models plotted in Figure 2, not 'six models including PaliGemma2'.
